newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Only seven more years in prison for Cali kingpins?.
newsitem.headline: Only seven more years in prison for Cali kingpins?.

text.p: The two brothers who led Colombia's Cali drug cartel will be sentenced this month to prison terms that could see them freed in as little as seven years, a judicial source said on Friday.

Two sources close to chief prosecutor Alfonso Valdivieso said Gilberto and Miguel Rodriguez Orejuela had confessed this week to the drug-related charge of illicit enrichment and to multiple counts of fraud stemming from the use of bank accounts opened in the name of corporate fronts to handle the proceeds from their illicit drug empire.

The brothers, reputed billionaires, also agreed to pay fines totalling $162 million, the sources said. Their confessions were made as part of an elaborate plea bargain struck with Valdevieso's office, they said.
U.S. officials believe they continue to direct the world's largest drug-trafficking organisation from prison.

The Colombian sources said two "faceless" or anonymous judges in Bogota would decide whether to impose the maximum sentences of 24 years that prosecutors have requested for the brothers. The ruling is likely to come within the next two weeks, they added.

The brothers face separate sentencing on drug-trafficking charges by a judge in the southwestern city of Cali. That sentence would also total no more than 24 years and must be served concurrently with the one handed down in Bogota.

Under Colombian law, the Rodriguezes' sentences would automatically be reduced by a third -- to 16 years -- because the brothers have cooperated with judicial officials and confessed to some of their crimes.

Additional time would be taken off for good behaviour, the sources said. But they disagreed on how much. One source said the 16 years could be halved, to eight; the other said no more than three years was likely to be shaved off, leaving 13.

In either event, the brothers would be credited with the time they have already spent in custody -- more than a year. This means that Gilberto Rodriguez, known as "the Chess Player" and the cartel's mastermind, could conceivably celebrate his 65 birthday in January 2004 as a free man.

The government of President Ernesto Samper, bowing to pressure from the United States, has proposed legislation setting stiffer penalties for drug trafficking, but any tougher sentences that might be approved by lawmakers would not be retroactive, nor would a possible move to lift Colombia's constitutional ban on extradition.

Both Rodriguezes are both targets of U.S. extradition requests. Gilberto was arrested in June 1995 and Miguel two months later in a nationwide sweep against the organisation that once controlled 80 percent of the world's cocaine trade.

Miguel, 53 years old and apparently a model prisoner, is studying business administration and English at Bogota's La Picota prison. He has opened a stand in the prison yard from which he sells fellow inmates items such as soda, chocolate, toilet paper, toy cars and cookies.
Gilberto, who has a cell near his brother's, is also studying English.
